This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.0`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noVueRequiredPropWithDefault`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**warning**](/reference/diagnostics#warning).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`vue/no-required-prop-with-default`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/no-required-prop-with-default)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueRequiredPropWithDefault": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow props that are both required and have a default value.

A prop with a default value can be omitted, because Vue falls back to the default value.
Marking such a prop as required is contradictory: parent components are expected to always
pass a required prop, so its default value should never be needed.

This rule checks props declared with the `props` option, with `defineProps()`, and with
type-based `defineProps<T>()` whose defaults are provided through `withDefaults()` or
props destructuring.

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    name: string;
  }>(),
  {
    name: "Foo",
  },
);
</script>
```

### Valid

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    name?: string;
    age: number;
  }>(),
  {
    name: "Foo",
  },
);
</script>
```

```vue
<script setup>
const props = defineProps({
  name: {
    required: false,
    default: "Foo",
  },
  age: {
    required: true,
  },
});
</script>
```
